# ADR-1115: One pipeline for every pull request, run by the Claude bot

## Status

accepted

## Context

Cortex's ci.yml grew to 1,300 lines of per-job workflows (test matrix on PostgreSQL, SQLite, mcp-host-config, docker smoke, install-e2e, release gate) plus separate Claude review workflows (claude.yml, claude-review.yml). The owner decided on 2026-10-22 (zetetic-team-subagents, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-single-ci-design.md, decisions 1 to 9) that the eight repositories share one pipeline of identical shape, generated from one template: unit tests with a 90 % line-coverage floor read from a Cobertura coverage.xml, non-regression tests, end-to-end tests, environment tests and installation tests on bare ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners (the GitHub image plus the pinned Claude Code CLI 2.1.296, nothing else), then the Claude bot's review and fix (anthropics/claude-code-action at a5a423f, the code-review plugin invoked as `/code-review:code-review --comment`, then a fix step), then a squash auto-merge, and a release tag from main. The per-repository contract is ci.json with exactly the keys unit, regression, e2e, environment, install and an optional version_file. An empty step is a failure. Measured on claude-mods #38 and session-optimizer #73 the same day: a merge job whose `if:` is not met is skipped, and GitHub treats a skipped required check as satisfied, so the merge job must fail explicitly. The bot's App token lacks the `workflows` scope, so a workflow change is never a bot commit, and PRs that touch pipeline.yml get no bot review (the action refuses a workflow that differs from main). Cortex's own release gate (ci.yml:1150-1280, ADR-0802) is the tag job of the template; Cortex keeps `scripts/doc_claim_sources.canonical_version` (pyproject.toml) as its version source and the check_version_surfaces step. Alternatives considered: the centralised reusable workflow of PR #780 (rejected by the design: each repository owns a full copy, nothing is called from another repository at run time); keeping per-repository exceptions in the pipeline (rejected: a repository that lacks a step is red until it has the step).

## Decision

Cortex adds .github/workflows/pipeline.yml (name "Pipeline", the bootstrap render of the zetetic-team-subagents template) and ci.json, and deletes claude-review.yml (its review job replaces it; claude.yml, the @claude mention, stays). The pipeline's jobs are contract, unit, regression, e2e, environment (matrix ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest), install (same matrix, fresh HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), review, merge and tag, in that dependency order. ci.json: unit runs the SQLite-backed pytest suite under uv with `--cov=mcp_server --cov-report=xml`; regression runs tests_py/integration on SQLite; e2e runs scripts/docker_smoke.sh (building the image); environment installs the project into a fresh virtual environment and runs cortex-doctor; install runs scripts/install_e2e/run.py against the checkout as marketplace, on the three OS; version_file is pyproject.toml. No mutation run is part of the pipeline (owner rule 2026-10-22: mutation testing is scoped to the files a PR changes, never a whole tree). The merge job runs on every same-repo, non-draft pull request and its first step fails, naming the job, when unit, regression, e2e, environment or install is not a success or review failed; only then does it arm `gh pr merge --auto --squash`, with no checkout. The review job is skipped, keyed on the head SHA, when the head commit is authored by claude[bot], when the diff touches pipeline.yml, on drafts, forks and Dependabot. The existing ci.yml and the other workflows are not changed by the bootstrap PR; their retirement is a later decision. The 90 % floor is a red cell for Cortex (82 % today, ci.yml's --cov-fail-under=82), as is the new Windows leg of install.

## Consequences

Easier: one pipeline shape across the eight repositories, drift visible in the generated header; a PR merges only when the five test steps are green on the commit the bot last pushed; a skipped merge can no longer pass as satisfied; the bot owns review and fix end to end. Harder: the pipeline reports red cells the product must fix (coverage under 90 %, the Windows install leg); the ubuntu test jobs install their own toolchain inside the ci.json commands (uv via pipx) because the pipeline sets up no stack; the docker smoke rebuilds the image on every run (no GHA layer cache in the generic pipeline); bootstrap and template-bump PRs carry no bot review and must be checked by their own run. Source lines: pipeline.yml cites this ADR; the tag job keeps ADR-0802's release-gate logic.
